sa-1.prompt: A sagittal plane divides the human body into which two parts?
sa-1.explanation: A sagittal plane runs vertically front-to-back to divide the body into left and right portions.

sa-2.prompt: What is the functional filtration unit of the kidney?
sa-2.explanation: Each kidney contains roughly 1 million nephrons responsible for filtration, reabsorption, and secretion.

sa-3.prompt: Which type of muscle tissue is striated and involuntary?
sa-3.explanation: Cardiac muscle exhibits striations and intercalated discs under involuntary autonomic control.

sa-4.prompt: Normal resting adult cardiac output averages approximately:
sa-4.explanation: Cardiac Output = Heart Rate × Stroke Volume, averaging 4–8 L/min at rest.

sa-5.prompt: Which blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?
sa-5.explanation: The pulmonary arteries are the only arteries in postnatal circulation carrying deoxygenated blood.

sa-6.prompt: Which cranial nerve mediates the sense of hearing and equilibrium?
sa-6.explanation: CN VIII transmits cochlear (auditory) and vestibular (balance) signals.

sa-7.prompt: The pacemaker that normally initiates every cardiac electrical impulse is the:
sa-7.explanation: The sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium fires at 60–100 bpm as the natural pacemaker.

sa-8.prompt: What is the normal lifespan of a human erythrocyte (red blood cell)?
sa-8.explanation: Mature erythrocytes circulate for ~120 days before splenic macrophages clear them.

sa-9.prompt: Intrinsic factor, essential for vitamin B12 absorption, is secreted by which cells of the stomach?
sa-9.explanation: Gastric parietal cells secrete both hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor.

sa-10.prompt: Primary gas exchange of O2 and CO2 occurs across which respiratory structure?
sa-10.explanation: Thin Type I pneumocytes and capillary endothelium allow rapid O2/CO2 diffusion across alveoli.

sa-11.prompt: Which chamber of the heart receives oxygenated blood directly from the four pulmonary veins?
sa-11.explanation: Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs via four pulmonary veins into the left atrium.

sa-12.prompt: Which endocrine gland releases antidiuretic hormone (ADH) and oxytocin into systemic circulation?
sa-12.explanation: Hypothalamic neurons synthesize ADH and oxytocin, which are stored and released by the posterior pituitary.

sa-13.prompt: In the anatomical position, the palms of the hands are facing:
sa-13.explanation: Standard anatomical position: standing upright, feet parallel, arms at sides, palms facing forward.

sa-14.prompt: Bile is synthesized by hepatocytes in the liver and concentrated in the:
sa-14.explanation: The liver produces bile; the gallbladder stores and concentrates it until fat enters the duodenum.

sa-15.prompt: Which organelle is primarily responsible for ATP synthesis via aerobic cellular respiration?
sa-15.explanation: Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.

sa-16.prompt: Which lobe of the cerebral cortex processes primary visual input from the optic tracts?
sa-16.explanation: The occipital lobe at the posterior cerebrum houses the primary visual cortex.

sa-17.prompt: Which heart valve prevents backflow from the left ventricle into the left atrium during ventricular systole?
sa-17.explanation: The mitral (bicuspid) valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle and closes tightly during systole.

sa-18.prompt: Which bone forms the posterior-inferior portion of the cranial base surrounding the foramen magnum?
sa-18.explanation: The occipital bone encloses the foramen magnum where the spinal cord exits the skull.

sa-19.prompt: Where are digestive enzymes such as amylase, lipase, and trypsinogen produced?
sa-19.explanation: Pancreatic acinar cells secrete amylase, lipase, and proteases into the duodenum.

sa-20.prompt: Which adult radial pulse rate should the nurse document as tachycardia?
sa-20.explanation: Normal adult resting pulse is 60–100 bpm; > 100 bpm is tachycardia.

sa-21.prompt: When cleaning a non-infected surgical incision, the nurse should wipe:
options: From the outer edges inward toward the incision
Directly back and forth along the same swab
From the cleanest area (incision) outward to surrounding skin
Circularly starting at the drain site toward the suture line
sa-21.explanation: Sterile wound cleansing always moves from cleanest (least contaminated) to dirtiest area.

sa-22.prompt: When removing sterile PPE, which item is normally contaminated most and removed FIRST?
sa-22.explanation: Gloves carry highest surface contamination and are removed first to avoid contaminating skin/face.

sa-23.prompt: How long should a nurse scrub hands with soap and running water during routine hygienic handwashing?
sa-23.explanation: WHO guidelines specify 40–60 seconds for soap-and-water handwashing (20–30s for alcohol rub).

sa-24.prompt: According to WHO 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene, when must alcohol hand rub or soap washing occur?
options: Before patient contact, before aseptic task, after body fluid exposure, after patient contact & surroundings
sa-24.explanation: All 5 WHO moments prevent healthcare-associated infections.

sa-25.prompt: When collecting a clean-catch midstream urine culture specimen, the patient should:
options: Collect the very first drops of urine
Void a small amount into toilet first, then catch midstream in sterile cup
Add tap water to dilute concentrated urine
sa-25.explanation: Voiding initially flushes distal urethral flora so midstream reflects bladder urine.

sa-26.prompt: Contact precautions (gown + gloves) are specifically mandatory for which condition?
options: MRSA wound infection or Clostridioides difficile diarrhea
sa-26.explanation: Contact precautions prevent direct/indirect transfer of MRSA, C. diff, or scabies.

sa-27.prompt: In documentation, if a medication dose was omitted because the patient vomited, the nurse should:
options: Leave the chart blank until tomorrow
Record the omission, reason, vitals, and provider notification accurately
Use correction fluid to erase the scheduled row
sa-27.explanation: Legal nursing records require factual, timely, non-erased documentation of omissions and rationale.

sa-28.prompt: What is the normal adult respiratory rate?

sa-29.prompt: For an adult ear otoscope exam, how should the nurse pull the pinna?
sa-29.explanation: Adult ear canal: pull pinna UP and BACK. In children under 3 years, pull DOWN and BACK.

sa-30.prompt: During an abdominal physical examination, what is the correct assessment sequence?
sa-30.explanation: Auscultate the abdomen BEFORE palpation/percussion so bowel sounds are not artificially altered or pain triggered.

sa-31.prompt: Which nursing intervention prevents pressure ulcers in an immobile stroke patient?
options: Reposition the patient at least every 2 hours
Elevate head of bed to 90 degrees continuously
Use donut-shaped air cushions under the sacrum
sa-31.explanation: Repositioning q2h relieves capillary occlusion; massaging reddened tissue worsens shear injury.

sa-32.prompt: Which thermometer route provides the closest core body temperature but is contraindicated in neutropenia or cardiac arrhythmia?
sa-32.explanation: Rectal temperature reflects core heat accurately but risks mucosal trauma or vagal bradycardia.

sa-33.prompt: Which assessment finding demonstrates objective rather than subjective data?
options: Measured blood pressure 88/54 mmHg and diaphoresis
sa-33.explanation: Measured vitals and observable physical signs are objective data.

sa-34.prompt: Which patient position best relieves dyspnoea and improves lung expansion?
sa-34.explanation: High-Fowler's lowers the diaphragm via gravity and maximizes thoracic expansion.

sa-35.prompt: Which finding on pulse oximetry requires immediate clinical intervention?
sa-35.explanation: Normal SpO2 is 95–100%; < 90% signifies critical hypoxemia.

sa-36.prompt: Which step of the ADPIE nursing process comes immediately after Assessment?
sa-36.explanation: The 5 steps follow Assessment → Diagnosis → Planning → Implementation → Evaluation.

sa-37.prompt: A NANDA nursing diagnosis written in P-E-S format includes:
options: Problem, Etiology (Related to), Signs/Symptoms (As evidenced by)
sa-37.explanation: PES links the nursing Problem to its Etiology and observable Evidence.

sa-38.prompt: Which blood pressure reading meets criteria for adult hypertension (two separate readings)?
sa-38.explanation: BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg on repeated readings defines hypertension.

sa-39.prompt: What is the normal baseline fetal heart rate (FHR) range?
sa-39.explanation: Normal term fetal heart rate is 110–160 bpm.

sa-40.prompt: Which drug is first-line to prevent and stop eclamptic seizures in severe pre-eclampsia?
sa-40.explanation: Magnesium Sulfate is the WHO gold standard anticonvulsant in eclampsia/severe pre-eclampsia.

sa-41.prompt: What does a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg plus 3+ proteinuria at 34 weeks gestation indicate?
sa-41.explanation: Severe hypertension + proteinuria after 20 weeks = Severe Pre-eclampsia.

sa-42.prompt: Using Naegele's Rule, if LMP began on 10 March 2026, what is the Estimated Date of Delivery (EDD)?
sa-42.explanation: Naegele's Rule: LMP + 7 days + 9 months = March 10 + 7 days = March 17 + 9 months = Dec 17.

sa-43.prompt: At what cervical dilation does the Active Phase of First Stage of Labour begin on the modern partograph?
sa-43.explanation: Latent phase is 0–3 cm; Active phase runs from 4 cm to full 10 cm dilation.

sa-44.prompt: During an APGAR assessment at 1 minute, a newborn has pink body/blue extremities, HR 130, active crying, good flexion, and sneezes with suction. What is the APGAR score?
sa-44.explanation: Appearance (1 for acrocyanosis), Pulse (2), Grimace (2), Activity (2), Respiration (2) = 9/10.

sa-45.prompt: What is the recommended minimum duration for Exclusive Breastfeeding under WHO & Uganda MoH guidelines?
sa-45.explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months gives optimal nutrition, passive IgA immunity, and lactational amenorrhea support.

sa-46.prompt: In shoulder dystocia emergency, what is the immediate first maternal positioning maneuver?
options: McRoberts maneuver (hyperflex maternal thighs onto abdomen) + suprapubic pressure
sa-46.explanation: McRoberts flattens the sacral promontory and rotates the symphysis pubis upward; NEVER apply fundal pressure.

sa-47.prompt: When performing fundal massage for uterine atony, the uterus should feel:
options: Soft and boggy above the umbilicus
Firm like a contracted grapefruit in the midline
Deviated sharply to the right groin
sa-47.explanation: A firm contracted uterus compresses spiral arteries to arrest bleeding.

sa-48.prompt: Primary Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) is defined after vaginal delivery as blood loss equal to or greater than:
sa-48.explanation: PPH is ≥ 500 mL after vaginal birth (or ≥ 1,000 mL after cesarean section) within 24 hours.

sa-49.prompt: On a WHO Partograph, crossing the Action Line indicates:
options: Urgent medical intervention/review for prolonged or obstructed labour
sa-49.explanation: Crossing the Action Line (4 hours right of Alert Line) demands immediate obstetric intervention.

sa-50.prompt: Which fetal lie and presentation is safest and most common for spontaneous vaginal birth?
options: Longitudinal lie with cephalic vertex presentation
sa-50.explanation: Longitudinal lie with flexed vertex presentation presents the smallest suboccipitobregmatic diameter (9.5 cm).

sa-51.prompt: Which maneuver defines the Third Stage of Labour placental delivery?
options: Controlled Cord Traction (CCT) with uterine counter-traction
sa-51.explanation: Controlled Cord Traction while applying upward suprapubic counter-traction prevents uterine inversion.

sa-52.prompt: Painless bright-red vaginal bleeding in the third trimester (at 32 weeks) is classically suspicious for:
sa-52.explanation: Placenta previa causes painless bright-red bleeding; NEVER perform a digital vaginal exam before ultrasound rules it out.

sa-53.prompt: Before giving a maintenance dose of Magnesium Sulfate, what must the midwife verify?
options: Urine output ≥ 30 mL/hr, Respiratory rate ≥ 16/min, and present patellar reflex
sa-53.explanation: Loss of patellar reflex, RR < 16, or urine output < 30 mL/hr signals MgSO4 toxicity (antidote: Calcium Gluconate).

sa-54.prompt: What is the MOST common cause of primary postpartum hemorrhage (the leading 'T' of the 4 Ts)?
sa-54.explanation: Uterine atony accounts for ~70–80% of primary PPH cases.

sa-55.prompt: Under WHO/Uganda Active Management of Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL), what uterotonic is given immediately after delivery of the baby (after ruling out twins)?
sa-55.explanation: WHO recommends Oxytocin 10 IU IM within 1 minute of birth as the uterotonic of choice.

sa-56.prompt: In PMTCT (Option B+) in Uganda, HIV-positive pregnant mothers should:
options: Start or continue lifelong triple ART regardless of CD4 count
sa-56.explanation: Option B+ provides lifelong ART to suppress maternal viral load and prevent vertical transmission.

sa-57.prompt: Which vaccine is routinely given to pregnant mothers in Uganda to prevent neonatal tetanus?
sa-57.explanation: Td vaccination during pregnancy protects both mother and newborn via transplacental IgG antibodies.

sa-58.prompt: Which organ is the primary site of First-Pass Drug Metabolism for oral medications?
sa-58.explanation: Oral drugs enter the portal vein to the liver before reaching systemic circulation.

sa-59.prompt: Which antidote reverses acute opioid-induced respiratory depression?
sa-59.explanation: Naloxone is a competitive mu-opioid receptor antagonist.

sa-60.prompt: What electrolyte abnormality is caused by Furosemide (Loop diuretic) and increases Digoxin toxicity risk?
sa-60.explanation: Furosemide wastes K+; hypokalemia sensitizes myocardium to Digoxin toxicity.

sa-61.prompt: Which class of antihypertensives can cause dry persistent cough and angioedema by accumulating bradykinin?
sa-61.explanation: ACE inhibitors elevate bradykinin; switch to an ARB (e.g., Losartan) if dry cough develops.

sa-62.prompt: In the standard adult patient, a normal therapeutic INR range for Warfarin anticoagulation is typically:
sa-62.explanation: Most DVT/PE/AF indications target INR 2.0–3.0; excess INR is reversed with Vitamin K.

sa-63.prompt: Which medication is contraindicated in pregnancy because it causes fetal teratogenic neural/kidney defects or premature ductus closure?
sa-63.explanation: Warfarin and ACE inhibitors are teratogenic; switch anticoagulation to LMWH/Heparin and HTN to Methyldopa/Nifedipine.

sa-64.prompt: Which bronchodilator provides rapid rescue relief during an acute asthma attack?
sa-64.explanation: Salbutamol relaxes bronchial smooth muscle within minutes.

sa-65.prompt: Why should patients taking Metronidazole strictly avoid alcohol?
sa-65.explanation: Metronidazole inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, triggering severe disulfiram reactions with alcohol.

sa-66.prompt: A nurse reconstitutes Ceftriaxone 1g with 10 mL sterile water. How many mL contain a prescribed 500 mg dose?

sa-67.prompt: For an adult experiencing acute anaphylactic shock, what is the immediate first-line drug and route?
options: Epinephrine (Adrenaline) 0.5 mg IM (1:1000) into anterolateral thigh
sa-67.explanation: IM Epinephrine 1:1000 into the mid-outer thigh is life-saving in anaphylaxis.

sa-68.prompt: 1,000 mL Normal Saline is ordered over 8 hours using a macrodrip set of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate?

sa-69.prompt: Which oral anti-TB drug turns urine, tears, and sweat harmlessly orange-red?
sa-69.explanation: Counsel TB patients that Rifampicin turns body fluids orange-red and reduces oral contraceptive efficacy.

sa-70.prompt: Which insulin has the fastest onset (10–15 minutes) and must be given right before eating?
sa-70.explanation: Rapid-acting analogs peak within 1–2h; never administer unless meal is present.

sa-71.prompt: Which oral antibiotic stains developing teeth and impairs bone growth in children under 8 years and pregnant women?
sa-71.explanation: Tetracyclines chelate calcium in developing teeth and fetal bone.

sa-72.prompt: Which medication is first-line for Severe Uncomplicated & Complicated Malaria in Uganda (parenteral)?
sa-72.explanation: IV/IM Artesunate is Uganda Clinical Guidelines first-line treatment for severe malaria.

sa-73.prompt: Which organ failure prolongs drug half-life most dangerously for aminoglycosides like Gentamicin?
sa-73.explanation: Gentamicin is almost exclusively renally excreted and is nephrotoxic/ototoxic.

sa-74.prompt: A prescriber orders 500 mg Amoxicillin PO. Stock tablets are 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?

sa-75.prompt: Before administering Digoxin to a cardiac patient, the nurse checks apical pulse for 1 full minute and holds the dose if pulse is:
sa-75.explanation: Hold Digoxin if adult apical HR < 60 bpm or signs of toxicity (yellow halos, nausea) appear.

sa-76.prompt: Which adverse effect should nurses monitor for with Isoniazid (INH), prevented by Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?
sa-76.explanation: Give Pyridoxine (Vit B6) alongside Isoniazid to prevent peripheral neuropathy.

sa-77.prompt: Using the Wallace Rule of Nines, what is the burn %TBSA of an adult with burns over the entire anterior trunk and entire right leg?
sa-77.explanation: Anterior trunk = 18% + Entire right leg = 18% = 36% TBSA.

sa-78.prompt: Using the Parkland Formula (4 mL × kg × %TBSA), how much fluid is needed in the FIRST 8 hours for a 70 kg adult with a 20% burn?
sa-78.explanation: Total 24h = 4 × 70 × 20 = 5,600 mL; 50% is given in the first 8 hours = 2,800 mL.

sa-79.prompt: Which ECG finding demands immediate defibrillation (shockable cardiac arrest rhythm)?
sa-79.explanation: Shockable rhythms are V-fib and pulseless V-tach; Asystole/PEA require CPR + Epinephrine (not shock).

sa-80.prompt: Rebound tenderness at McBurney's point in the Right Lower Quadrant is classic for:
sa-80.explanation: McBurney's point sits 1/3 the distance from right ASIS to umbilicus.

sa-81.prompt: A patient presents with sudden severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and serum amylase 4× normal. Suspect:
sa-81.explanation: Elevated amylase/lipase > 3× normal + epigastric pain radiating to back = Acute Pancreatitis.

sa-82.prompt: What does Trousseau's sign (carpal spasm on BP cuff inflation) or Chvostek's sign indicate?
sa-82.explanation: Neuromuscular excitability after thyroidectomy signals hypocalcemia (low PTH).

sa-83.prompt: Which sign confirms suspected meningitis on bedside physical exam?
options: Nuchal rigidity (neck stiffness), Kernig's & Brudzinski's signs + fever
sa-83.explanation: Meningeal irritation triggers nuchal rigidity, positive Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs.

sa-84.prompt: In benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) causing acute urinary retention, the priority nursing action is:
options: Insert a urinary catheter (Foley) under strict asepsis to decompress bladder
sa-84.explanation: Decompress bladder smoothly; monitor for post-obstructive diuresis.

sa-85.prompt: A patient with COPD should receive oxygen titrated carefully (target SpO2 88–92%) because excess oxygen can:
options: Blunt hypoxic respiratory drive and worsen CO2 retention
sa-85.explanation: Controlled low-flow O2 prevents hypercapnic narcosis in chronic CO2 retainers.

sa-86.prompt: In a patient with an acute ischemic stroke, what must be obtained BEFORE considering thrombolytic therapy?
options: Non-contrast Head CT scan to rule out intracranial hemorrhage
sa-86.explanation: Hemorrhagic vs ischemic stroke look identical clinically; CT rules out bleed.

sa-87.prompt: What is the FIRST priority intervention for a patient arriving in Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
options: IV isotonic Normal Saline (0.9% NaCl) fluid resuscitation
sa-87.explanation: Restore intravascular volume with IV 0.9% NaCl first, followed by IV Regular Insulin + K+ monitoring.

sa-88.prompt: Pain out of proportion to injury, tense swollen limb, paresthesia, and pain on passive stretch after a tibial fracture signify:
sa-88.explanation: Compartment syndrome threatens limb ischemia; loosen tight casts immediately and notify surgeon for fasciotomy.

sa-89.prompt: Which nursing care step is vital for a patient with a closed chest tube drainage system (water-seal)?
options: Clamp the tube continuously during transport
Keep the drainage chamber below chest level and monitor gentle tidaling
Raise the drainage bottle above the bed
Empty the water-seal fluid every hour
sa-89.explanation: Never clamp routinely; keep below chest level to prevent fluid reflux and tension pneumothorax.

sa-90.prompt: When caring for an acute upper GI bleed (hematemesis / melena), the immediate nurse priority is:
options: Assess airway, establish 2 large-bore IV lines, crossmatch blood, and give isotonic fluids
sa-90.explanation: Stabilize Airway and Circulation (fluids/PRBCs) first; avoid NSAIDs.

sa-91.prompt: Which clinical sign indicates impending Hypovolemic or Compensated Septic Shock?
options: Narrowing pulse pressure, tachycardia, cool extremities, capillary refill > 3s
sa-91.explanation: Sympathetic vasoconstriction causes tachycardia, cool clammy skin, and rising diastolic pressure initially.

sa-92.prompt: Which assessment sign suggests right-sided Heart Failure rather than isolated left-sided Heart Failure?
options: Jugular venous distention (JVD), hepatomegaly, and bilateral ankle edema
sa-92.explanation: Right heart failure backs up into systemic veins (JVD, liver congestion, peripheral edema).

sa-93.prompt: Which classic triad characterizes Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
options: Hyperglycemia, ketosis/ketonuria, and metabolic acidosis (Kussmaul breathing)
sa-93.explanation: DKA presents with hyperglycemia, ketone production, and high anion-gap metabolic acidosis.

sa-94.prompt: Murphy's sign (inspiratory arrest when palpating right upper quadrant under costal margin) points to:
sa-94.explanation: Painful arrest when the inflamed gallbladder touches palpating fingers indicates cholecystitis.

sa-95.prompt: Which cardiac biomarker is most specific and remains elevated longest (7–10 days) after acute Myocardial Infarction?
sa-95.explanation: Cardiac Troponin I/T rises within 3–6 hours and stays elevated 7–10 days.

sa-96.prompt: Which MUAC (Mid-Upper Arm Circumference) measurement in a 2-year-old child indicates Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)?
sa-96.explanation: MUAC < 11.5 cm (or bilateral pitting oedema) defines Severe Acute Malnutrition.

sa-97.prompt: What is the key nutritional hallmark distinguishing Kwashiorkor from Marasmus?
options: Marked bilateral pitting edema, hepatomegaly, flaky-paint dermatitis & 'moon face'
Extreme severe muscle/fat wasting ('skin and bones') with alert hungry appearance
sa-97.explanation: Kwashiorkor is protein-deficiency oedematous malnutrition; Marasmus is total calorie wasting.

sa-98.prompt: What is the preferred first-line antibiotic for non-severe Pneumonia in Ugandan children aged 2–59 months?
options: Oral Amoxicillin dispersible tablets (DT) for 5 days
sa-98.explanation: Uganda MoH / WHO IMCI recommends high-dose oral Amoxicillin DT for outpatient pediatric pneumonia.

sa-99.prompt: For a preterm low-birth-weight newborn in Uganda, Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) primarily prevents:
options: Hypothermia, hypoglycemia, and neonatal sepsis while promoting weight gain
sa-99.explanation: Skin-to-skin KMC stabilizes temperature, supports breastfeeding, and improves preterm survival.

sa-100.prompt: Which sign distinguishes Pneumonia from a simple cough/cold in a 10-month-old infant under IMCI?
options: Fast breathing (>= 50 breaths/min for age 2–11 months) or lower chest wall indrawing

sa-101.prompt: Which finding on physical exam of a newborn should prompt suspicion of Congenital Heart Disease?
options: Central cyanosis (tongue/lips), tachypnea with sweating during feeds, and loud heart murmur
sa-101.explanation: Central cyanosis and feeding fatigue point to congenital cardiac shunts or failure.

sa-102.prompt: What does the Pentavalent vaccine protect Ugandan infants against?
options: Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)
Malaria, Typhoid, Cholera, Yellow Fever, Rabies
sa-102.explanation: DPT-HepB-Hib is given at 6, 10, and 14 weeks of age.

sa-103.prompt: In Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) during the initial stabilization phase (F-75), why must high-protein/high-iron feeds be avoided initially?
options: They cause weight gain too slowly
Liver/renal organs cannot handle excess protein/sodium/iron yet (risks heart failure & refeeding shock)
sa-103.explanation: Start with F-75 cautiously and wait to add Iron until the Rehabilitation (F-100 / RUTF) phase after infections clear.

sa-104.prompt: Phototherapy is used to treat Neonatal Jaundice primarily to prevent bilirubin-induced encephalopathy known as:
sa-104.explanation: Unconjugated bilirubin crosses the infant blood-brain barrier and causes irreversible Kernicterus.

sa-105.prompt: When resuscitating a newborn who is not breathing and has HR < 100 bpm after drying & stimulation, what is the FIRST priority within the Golden Minute?
options: Positive-Pressure Ventilation (Bag-and-Mask) at 40–60 breaths/min with room air
sa-105.explanation: Ventilating newborn lungs with bag-and-mask within 60 seconds is the #1 resuscitation action.

sa-106.prompt: Under the UNEPI (Uganda National Expanded Programme on Immunization) schedule, which vaccines are given at BIRTH?
options: BCG (right upper arm ID) and OPV 0
sa-106.explanation: At birth: BCG intradermally + OPV 0 oral.

sa-107.prompt: Which clinical sign defines Severe Malaria in a child rather than uncomplicated malaria?
options: Prostration, convulsions, impaired consciousness, severe anemia (Hb < 5 g/dL), or hypoglycemia
sa-107.explanation: Cerebral malaria / severe anemia / respiratory distress require parenteral IV Artesunate immediately.

sa-108.prompt: Which classic symptom characterizes Croup (Acute Laryngotracheobronchitis) in toddlers?
options: Inspiratory stridor and a harsh 'barking seal' cough worse at night
sa-108.explanation: Subglottic edema in parainfluenza virus produces barking cough and stridor (treat with Dexamethasone).

sa-109.prompt: Which intervention lowers neonatal umbilical cord infection risk in home or rural deliveries?
options: Chlorhexidine 7.1% gel / dry clean cord care
Tightly wrapping the cord in plastic
sa-109.explanation: Chlorhexidine cord care and clean dry care prevent deadly neonatal tetanus and omphalitis.

sa-110.prompt: In Uganda Clinical Guidelines, what is the first-line management for a child with Moderate (Some) Dehydration from acute diarrhea?
options: Low-osmolarity ORS (75 mL/kg over 4 hours) + Zinc supplementation (10–20 mg/day for 10–14 days)
sa-110.explanation: Never give antimotility drugs in children; give ORS + Zinc 20 mg/day (10 mg if < 6 months).

sa-111.prompt: At what age is the first Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine routinely administered in Uganda?
sa-111.explanation: MR is administered subcutaneously at 9 months (and booster at 18 months).

sa-112.prompt: According to Uganda IMCI guidelines, which finding is an immediate General Danger Sign requiring urgent Pink hospital referral?
options: Convulsions, lethargy/unconsciousness, vomiting everything, or unable to drink/breastfeed
sa-112.explanation: Any General Danger Sign classifies as Severe Disease (Pink) requiring pre-referral care and urgent transfer.

sa-113.prompt: When assessing a sick infant aged 2 months to 5 years for Dehydration, which signs confirm SEVERE dehydration?
options: Lethargic/unconscious, sunken eyes, unable to drink, skin pinch goes back VERY slowly (> 2 seconds)
sa-113.explanation: Two or more severe dehydration signs demand immediate Plan C IV Ringer's Lactate resuscitation.

sa-114.prompt: What is the correct chest compression to ventilation ratio when performing CPR on a neonate with HR < 60 bpm despite 30s effective PPV?
sa-114.explanation: Neonatal resuscitation uses a 3:1 compression-to-ventilation ratio.

sa-115.prompt: What color do Gram-positive bacteria appear under a microscope after standard Gram staining?
sa-115.explanation: Thick peptidoglycan retains crystal violet-iodine complex, staining purple.

sa-116.prompt: Which acid-fast stain (Ziehl-Neelsen) is used to identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum?
options: Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB) pink/red rods on blue background
sa-116.explanation: Mycolic acid cell walls retain carbol fuchsin despite acid-alcohol decolorization.

sa-117.prompt: What is the cornerstone diagnostic test for Schistosoma mansoni (intestinal bilharzia common around Lake Victoria)?
sa-117.explanation: S. mansoni ova have a characteristic lateral spine (treat with Praziquantel).

sa-118.prompt: A sudden sharp spike of cholera cases above normal endemic baseline within a single district is defined as an:
sa-118.explanation: Epidemic = cases clearly exceeding expected baseline in a region; Pandemic = multi-continental spread.

sa-119.prompt: Bloody mucoid diarrhea with tenesmus and fever is classically caused by:
sa-119.explanation: Invasive Shigella damages colonic mucosa causing bloody diarrhea.

sa-120.prompt: When handling used syringes/needles on the ward, nurses must:
options: Recap every needle using two hands
Drop uncapped needle immediately into a puncture-proof yellow Sharps Box
sa-120.explanation: Never recap needles; fill sharps boxes only 3/4 full before sealing.

sa-121.prompt: Under Uganda color-coded medical waste segregation, infectious/anatomical clinical waste goes into which bin?
sa-121.explanation: Black = general waste; Yellow = infectious waste/sharps box; Red = highly infectious/anatomical.

sa-122.prompt: In epidemiology, what does 'Incidence Rate' specifically measure?
options: All existing cases (old + new) at a point in time
NEW cases developing in a population at risk during a defined period
sa-122.explanation: Incidence = new cases over time; Prevalence = total existing old + new cases.

sa-123.prompt: Which viral hepatitis forms are primarily spread via contaminated food/water (fecal-oral) rather than blood/sex?
sa-123.explanation: HAV and HEV spread fecal-orally (HEV carries high mortality in pregnancy).

sa-124.prompt: Autoclaving sterilizes surgical instruments by using pressurized saturated steam at:
sa-124.explanation: Moist heat at 121°C under pressure destroys bacteria, viruses, and heat-resistant endospores.

sa-125.prompt: At which health facility level in Uganda does the Village Health Team (VHT) operate?

es-free-1.prompt:
(a) Explain the fluid recovery mechanism between blood capillaries and lymphatic vessels. (4 marks)
(b) Describe three ways lymph nodes contribute to host immunity during peripheral tissue infection. (6 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Fluid filters continuously from arterial blood capillaries into interstitial tissue spaces; ~85% is reabsorbed directly into venous capillaries (2 marks).

(a) Remaining ~15% (2–4 litres/day) and escaped plasma proteins enter blind-ended lymphatic capillaries and return to central venous circulation via thoracic/right lymphatic ducts, preventing tissue oedema (2 marks).
(b) Afferent lymphatics route tissue fluid carrying microbes, cellular debris, and antigens through subcapsular and medullary sinuses where phagocytic macrophages engulf pathogens (2 marks).
(b) Antigen-presenting cells activate B-lymphocytes (in germinal centres -> plasma cells/antibodies) and T-lymphocytes (paracortex cell-mediated immunity) (2 marks).
(b) Slow flow across reticular trabeculae maximises pathogen trapping before filtered lymph exits via efferent vessels; nodal swelling indicates active immune proliferation (2 marks).
es-free-1.modelAnswer:
(a) At the microvascular bed, hydrostatic pressure forces plasma water and solutes into interstitial spaces. Approximately 85% of this filtered fluid is drawn back directly by capillary colloid osmotic pressure. The remaining 15%—roughly 2–4 litres per day alongside large escaped plasma proteins—cannot re-enter blood capillaries easily and therefore enters overlapping endothelial mini-valves of lymphatic capillaries. From there, lymph travels through collecting trunks and the thoracic duct back into the subclavian veins, maintaining circulating blood volume and preventing interstitial oedema.

(b) First, resident macrophages lining the lymph node sinuses phagocytose bacteria and cellular debris delivered by afferent lymphatic vessels. Second, trabeculae and reticular fibres slow lymph transit time, filtering pathogens before fluid reaches the venous circulation. Third, lymphocytes concentrated inside the cortex (B-cells in germinal centres and T-cells in the paracortex) recognise microbial antigens and mount both antibody-mediated (humoral) and cell-mediated immune responses.
es-free-1.examinerTip: Always state the quantitative split (85% blood capillary reabsorption vs 15% / 2–4 L/day lymphatic return) and mention prevention of oedema to earn full marks in UNMEB Anatomy Section B.

es-free-2.prompt:
(a) State the five (5) anatomical types of bones giving one human example for each. (5 marks)
(b) Outline five neurovascular observations ('5 Ps') a nurse monitors in a patient with a suspected limb fracture. (5 marks)
markingPoints: (a) 1 mark each (0.5 type + 0.5 correct example): Long bone (Femur/Humerus), Short bone (Carpals/Tarsals), Flat bone (Sternum/Scapula/Ribs/Cranium), Irregular bone (Vertebrae/Pelvic hip bone), Sesamoid bone (Patella).

(b) 1 mark per explained P: Pain (severe escalating pain out of proportion on passive stretch), Pallor (pale distal skin/nail beds), Pulselessness (diminished or absent distal arterial pulse e.g. dorsalis pedis), Paraesthesia (numbness/tingling sensory loss), Paralysis/Paresis (inability to move distal digits).
es-free-2.modelAnswer:
(a) Bones are classified into five morphological types:
1. Long bones — e.g. femur or humerus (longer than wide, act as levers).
2. Short bones — e.g. carpals or tarsals (cube-shaped, provide stability).
3. Flat bones — e.g. sternum, ribs, or parietal skull bones (thin plates protecting organs).
4. Irregular bones — e.g. vertebrae (complex shapes with projections).
5. Sesamoid bones — e.g. patella (embedded within tendons to alter mechanical pull).

(b) To detect compartment syndrome or arterial injury early, assess the '5 Ps' distal to the fracture every 15–30 minutes:
1. Pain: Persistent, escalating pain not relieved by elevation/analgesia.
2. Pallor: Cool, pale, or cyanotic skin indicating poor capillary perfusion.
3. Pulselessness: Absent or weak distal pulse (e.g. dorsalis pedis or radial) compared against the uninjured limb.
4. Paraesthesia: Pins-and-needles tingling or numbness from nerve compression.
5. Paralysis: Weakness or inability to flex/extend toes or fingers.
es-free-2.examinerTip: Never write just the single words 'Pain, Pallor...'; UNMEB markers deduct half-marks unless you briefly state how each sign is assessed distally.

es-free-3.topic: Emergency Nursing · Hypovolaemic Shock & ABCDE Resuscitation
es-free-3.prompt:
A 26-year-old patient arrives at Emergency Casualty after a road traffic crash with a deep femoral thigh laceration, active bleeding, cold clammy skin, BP 82/54 mmHg, Pulse 128 bpm, RR 28/min, and capillary refill 4 seconds.
(a) State the clinical condition presented and explain four compensatory vital-sign changes observed. (5 marks)
(b) Describe the immediate ABCDE nursing resuscitation priorities within the first 30 minutes. (10 marks)
(c) State two priority NANDA-style Nursing Diagnoses with one measurable outcome each. (5 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Hypovolaemic (haemorrhagic) shock — Decompensated/Class III haemorrhage (1 mark). Compensatory mechanisms: Tachycardia 128 bpm (sympathetic baroreceptor surge to sustain cardiac output), Tachypnoea 28/min (compensation for metabolic lactic acidosis/hypoxia), Delayed cap refill 4s & cold clammy skin (peripheral vasoconstriction shunting blood to heart/brain), Hypotension 82/54 mmHg (late loss of volume exceeding ~30% blood volume) (4 marks).

(b) Airway & C-spine protection + High-flow O2 via non-rebreather mask targeting SpO2 >= 94% (2 marks); Direct firm sterile pressure/haemostatic dressing on bleeding femoral laceration + elevate limb if no femur fracture contraindication (2 marks); Establish two large-bore 16G/18G IV cannulae + draw blood for grouping, cross-match, and baseline Hb (2 marks); Infuse warmed isotonic crystalloid (Ringer's Lactate or 0.9% NaCl bolus 20 mL/kg / 1–2 L rapidly) and prepare matched packed RBC transfusion (2 marks); Continuous monitoring of vitals q15m, urinary catheter for urine output targeting >= 0.5 mL/kg/hr (>= 30 mL/hr), and active warming blankets to prevent hypothermia/coagulopathy triad (2 marks).

(c) Diagnosis 1: Deficient Fluid Volume related to active arterial/venous haemorrhage as evidenced by BP 82/54 mmHg, HR 128 bpm, capillary refill 4s -> Outcome: Systolic BP >= 95–100 mmHg, HR < 100 bpm, urine output >= 30 mL/hr within 1–2 hours (2.5 marks). Diagnosis 2: Ineffective Tissue Perfusion (Peripheral/Cerebral) related to decreased circulating intravascular volume -> Outcome: Warm extremities, capillary refill < 2 seconds, alert orientation GCS 15/15 (2.5 marks).
es-free-3.modelAnswer:
(a) The patient is in acute hypovolaemic (haemorrhagic) shock secondary to acute blood loss. Sympathetic baroreceptors detect falling arterial pressure and trigger catecholamine release, causing compensatory tachycardia (128 bpm) to preserve cardiac output and peripheral vasoconstriction that makes skin cold and clammy and prolongs capillary refill (4 seconds). Tachypnoea (28/min) reflects cellular hypoxia and lactic acidosis. Hypotension (82/54 mmHg) confirms decompensated loss exceeding ~30% of blood volume.

(b) Immediate ABCDE resuscitation priorities:
• Airway & Breathing: Ensure airway patency (maintain cervical spine alignment if blunt trauma), apply high-flow oxygen (10–15 L/min via non-rebreather mask) targeting SpO2 94–98%.
• Circulation & Bleeding Control: Apply immediate direct firm sterile pressure over the bleeding laceration while assistants insert two large-bore (16G or 18G) peripheral IV cannulae. Withdraw samples immediately for blood grouping, cross-matching, and urgent haemoglobin.
• Fluid & Blood Resuscitation: Administer warmed isotonic crystalloid (Ringer's Lactate or 0.9% Sodium Chloride) rapidly while blood is cross-matched, monitoring chest auscultation for fluid overload.
• Disability & Exposure/Monitoring: Check GCS, insert an indwelling urinary catheter to ensure hourly urine output >= 30 mL/hr (>= 0.5 mL/kg/hr), cover with warm blankets to prevent trauma-induced hypothermia/coagulopathy, and escalate urgently for surgical theatre repair.

(c) Priority Nursing Diagnoses:
1. Deficient Fluid Volume related to active trauma haemorrhage as evidenced by hypotension (82/54 mmHg) and tachycardia (128 bpm). Expected Outcome: Client achieves SBP >= 100 mmHg, HR < 100 bpm, and urine output >= 30 mL/hr within 2 hours of fluid/blood therapy.
2. Ineffective Peripheral Tissue Perfusion related to reduced circulating blood volume as evidenced by cold clammy skin and 4-second capillary refill. Expected Outcome: Client displays warm skin and capillary refill < 2 seconds.
es-free-3.examinerTip: Structure trauma resuscitation questions strictly along ABCDE + 'Control external bleeding FIRST alongside two 16G/18G IV lines + urine output >= 30 mL/hr target'.

es-ms-1.prompt:
(a) State the first-line drug, loading schedule, and minimum duration of parenteral treatment for Severe Malaria under Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023. (4 marks)
(b) Explain three critical nursing safety checks when caring for a child or adult receiving IV Artesunate or Quinine. (6 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Drug: IV (or IM) Artesunate 2.4 mg/kg (or 3.0 mg/kg for children < 20 kg) at 0 hr, 12 hr, and 24 hr, then once every 24 hrs for a minimum of 24 hours (3 doses) until patient tolerates oral ACT (Artemether-Lumefantrine 3-day full course) (4 marks).
(b) Blood glucose monitoring every 4 hrs / anytime consciousness drops (malaria + quinine-stimulated hyperinsulinaemia cause severe hypoglycaemia < 2.5–3.0 mmol/L) (2 marks).

(b) Reconstitute Artesunate powder strictly with 5% sodium bicarbonate vial provided, dilute with 0.9% NaCl / 5% Dextrose, give slow IV bolus over 1–2 min immediately (do not store reconstituted solution) (2 marks).
(b) Monitor fluid balance/urine output for blackwater fever/AKI, control convulsions with IV/rectal Diazepam, and watch for delayed post-artesunate haemolysis 7–14 days post-discharge (2 marks).
es-ms-1.modelAnswer:
(a) Under Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023, IV Artesunate is first-line for severe malaria. Adults and children >= 20 kg receive 2.4 mg/kg IV (children < 20 kg receive 3.0 mg/kg) at Hours 0, 12, and 24, then once daily until oral feeding resumes, minimum 24 hours (3 parenteral doses), followed ALWAYS by a complete 3-day oral Artemether-Lumefantrine course.

(b) Nurses must perform three critical safety checks:
1. Capillary Blood Glucose Checks: Monitor RBG every 4 hours and immediately if confusion, sweating, or seizures occur, as severe falciparum parasitaemia and antimalarials (especially Quinine) rapidly trigger hypoglycaemia; treat unconscious hypoglycaemia promptly with 50% Dextrose (adults) or 10% Dextrose 2–5 mL/kg (children).
2. Correct Reconstitution & Immediate Administration: Dissolve Artesunate only with its accompanying 5% sodium bicarbonate ampoule, dilute properly, and inject slow IV immediately without storing leftovers.
3. Urine Output & Anaemia Monitoring: Chart strict input/output for dark 'Coca-Cola' urine (haemoglobinuria/AKI) and monitor pallor/Hb levels.
es-ms-1.examinerTip: Do not forget the weight distinction updated in recent WHO/UCG protocols: children under 20 kg receive 3.0 mg/kg Artesunate, while >= 20 kg receive 2.4 mg/kg.

es-ms-2.topic: Medical Pharmacology · Pulmonary TB DOTS Regimen
es-ms-2.prompt:
(a) Write out the standard first-line 6-month drug regimen (2RHZE / 4RH) for new drug-sensitive Pulmonary Tuberculosis, identifying all four medicines. (4 marks)
(b) State six patient counselling points on side-effects, adherence, and infection control. (6 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Intensive phase (2 months): Rifampicin (R), Isoniazid (H), Pyrazinamide (Z), Ethambutol (E) [2RHZE]; Continuation phase (4 months): Rifampicin + Isoniazid [4RH] daily (4 marks).

(b) 1 mark each: Harmless orange-red urine/tears discoloration (Rifampicin); Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) prevention of Isoniazid peripheral neuropathy; Immediate reporting of jaundice/RUQ pain/vomiting (hepatotoxicity from R/H/Z); Blurred vision/red-green colour blindness warning (Ethambutol optic neuritis); Strict daily DOTS adherence for full 6 months to prevent MDR-TB; Cough etiquette, wearing mask/covering mouth, ventilated sunlit rooms, screening household under-5 contacts.
es-ms-2.modelAnswer:
(a) Standard first-line anti-TB regimen is 2RHZE / 4RH: 2 months Intensive Phase of Rifampicin (R), Isoniazid (H), Pyrazinamide (Z), and Ethambutol (E) fixed-dose combination tablets taken daily, followed by 4 months Continuation Phase of Rifampicin and Isoniazid (RH).

(b) Patient education includes:
1. Reassure patient that Rifampicin harmlessly turns urine, sweat, and tears orange-red.
2. Advise completing Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) if co-prescribed to prevent Isoniazid numbness/tingling (peripheral neuropathy).
3. Instruct to stop drugs and return immediately if eyes turn yellow (jaundice), dark tea-like urine, or persistent vomiting occur (hepatotoxicity).
4. Report any blurred vision or colour-vision difficulty immediately (Ethambutol optic neuritis).
5. Never miss doses even after cough stops at 2 weeks — interrupting therapy drives Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB).
6. Practice cough hygiene, keep windows open for sunlight/ventilation, and bring household contacts (< 5 years / HIV+) for TB screening.
es-ms-2.examinerTip: Match each warning directly to the specific drug (Rifampicin -> orange secretions, Isoniazid -> neuropathy, Ethambutol -> vision, Pyrazinamide/R/H -> hepatitis).

es-ms-3.prompt:
(a) List four hallmark clinical and laboratory diagnostic features of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA). (4 marks)
(b) Describe three nursing management priorities in the first 4 hours of DKA treatment. (6 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Hyperglycaemia (often >= 11–13.9 mmol/L), Kussmaul deep rapid breathing / fruity acetone breath, Metabolic acidosis (pH < 7.3 / HCO3- < 15), Ketonuria/ketonaemia + severe dehydration (4 marks).

(b) Rehydration FIRST with 0.9% Sodium Chloride IV isotonic boluses before/during insulin (2 marks); Continuous IV Regular (Soluble) Insulin infusion while monitoring Serum Potassium K+ closely — insulin shifts K+ intracellularly risking fatal hypokalaemia/arrhythmia (2 marks); Hourly capillary glucose monitoring and switching IV fluid to 5% Dextrose once RBG falls <= 14 mmol/L to avoid cerebral oedema/hypoglycaemia (2 marks).
es-ms-3.modelAnswer:
(a) Hallmark DKA features: Blood glucose typically >= 13.9 mmol/L (250 mg/dL); significant ketonaemia or ketonuria; metabolic acidosis (arterial pH < 7.3, bicarbonate < 15 mEq/L); and Kussmaul deep laboured respirations with acetone ('fruity') breath odour plus polyuria/dehydration.

(b) Priority nursing actions:
1. Aggressive Isotonic Rehydration First: Infuse 0.9% Sodium Chloride IV to restore renal perfusion before insulin drops blood volume.
2. Regular Insulin & Potassium Safety: Prepare soluble regular insulin infusion ONLY after confirming urine output and checking Serum Potassium (K+ < 3.3 mmol/L requires K+ replacement before starting insulin to prevent fatal cardiac arrest).
3. Hourly RBG & Electrolyte Tracking: Measure blood glucose hourly and add Dextrose 5% IV once glucose drops around 14 mmol/L to prevent iatrogenic hypoglycaemia and cerebral oedema.
es-ms-3.examinerTip: UNMEB questions test the rule: NEVER start IV insulin if Serum Potassium is critically low (< 3.3 mmol/L) without potassium replacement!

es-ms-4.topic: Respiratory Medical Nursing · Severe Community Pneumonia & Oxygenation
es-ms-4.prompt:
Mr. K, 62 years old, is admitted with fever 39.2°C, productive rusty sputum, pleuritic right chest pain, RR 32 breaths/min, and SpO2 86% on room air. Chest radiograph shows right lower lobe consolidation.
(a) Explain the pathophysiology of hypoxaemia in lobar pneumonia. (4 marks)
(b) Detail eight (8) nursing interventions to improve oxygenation, clear secretions, and treat infection. (10 marks)
(c) Outline six discharge teaching points to prevent recurrence. (6 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Alveolar inflammatory exudate/pus fills right lower lobe air sacs, thickening the alveolar-capillary respiratory membrane, impairing O2 diffusion and creating ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) mismatch/intrapulmonary shunting -> arterial hypoxaemia SpO2 86% (4 marks).

(b) Semi-Fowler's/High-Fowler's upright positioning (1.25m); Titrated humidified O2 therapy targeting SpO2 94–98% (or 88–92% if COPD history) (1.25m); Collect sputum specimen for culture/GeneXpert BEFORE starting empiric IV antibiotics (Ceftriaxone + Azithromycin/Amoxicillin per UCG) (1.25m); Oral/IV hydration to thin viscous sputum (1.25m); Deep breathing exercises, chest physiotherapy & cautious coughing support (splinting painful chest) (1.25m); Antipyretic/analgesic for fever & pleuritic pain (Paracetamol, avoiding respiratory depressants) (1.25m); Frequent SpO2, RR, mental state checks q2–4h (1.25m); Droplet/standard infection control & isolation precautions (1.25m).

(c) Complete full oral antibiotic step-down course; Avoid smoking/indoor biomass cooking smoke; Hydrate well & nutrition-rich diet; Practice deep breathing; Annual/recommended vaccination (Pneumococcal/Influenza where indicated); Return early if recurrent fever, dyspnoea, or haemoptysis develops (6 marks).
es-ms-4.modelAnswer:
(a) Pathophysiology: Bacterial proliferation inside the right lower lobe triggers acute inflammatory hyperaemia and exudation of neutrophils, fibrin, and fluid into the alveoli (consolidation). Alveoli become airless and fluid-filled while capillary blood continues flowing past them, causing severe ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) mismatch and impaired oxygen diffusion across the thickened respiratory membrane, lowering arterial saturation to 86%.

(b) Priority Nursing Management:
1. Position upright in High-Fowler's (45–90°) to maximise diaphragm excursion.
2. Administer humidified supplemental oxygen via nasal prongs or simple/Venturi mask, titrating to SpO2 >= 94% (88–92% if underlying COPD exists).
3. Obtain sputum for microscopy/culture and blood cultures before timely administration of prescribed IV antibiotics (e.g. Ceftriaxone + Macrolide per UCG 2023).
4. Encourage adequate hydration (oral/IV fluids if no overload) to liquefy tenacious secretions.
5. Teach chest splinting with a pillow during coughing and coach deep breathing hourly.
6. Give Paracetamol to control high fever (39.2°C) and relieve pleuritic pain so deep breaths are comfortable.
7. Monitor RR, SpO2, pulse, and level of consciousness for sepsis/respiratory fatigue.
8. Enforce infection prevention (hand hygiene, safe sputum pot disposal).

(c) Discharge Education: Finish every prescribed tablet; stop tobacco/charcoal smoke exposure; keep hydrated and eat high-protein meals; continue breathing exercises; obtain recommended pneumococcal/influenza vaccines; seek urgent review if fever, chest pain, or breathlessness recurs.
es-ms-4.examinerTip: Mentioning sputum collection BEFORE first-dose IV antibiotic and safe SpO2 targets shows true clinical ward mastery.

es-mw-1.topic: Intrapartum Care · Active Management of Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL)
es-mw-1.prompt:
(a) Define Active Management of the Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL) and state its three core components. (4 marks)
(b) Explain three uterine checks a midwife performs immediately after placental delivery to prevent Postpartum Haemorrhage (PPH). (6 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Evidence-based bundle reducing postpartum haemorrhage by ~60% (1 mark). 3 components: 1) Uterotonic drug (Oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV within 1 minute of birth after ruling out second twin); 2) Controlled Cord Traction (CCT) with uterine counter-traction above symphysis pubis during contraction; 3) Uterine massage/assessment of tone immediately after placenta delivery (3 marks).

(b) 2 marks each: Palpate uterine fundus for firm globular contraction ('cricket ball') at or below umbilicus (treat atony immediately with massage/oxytocin); Inspect placenta & membranes thoroughly on flat surface for completeness (missing cotyledon/succenturiate lobe causes delayed PPH/sepsis); Inspect cervix, vagina, and perineum under bright light for genital tract trauma/tears and check cumulative blood loss + vital signs q15m x 2 hrs.
es-mw-1.modelAnswer:
(a) AMTSL is an essential preventive obstetric intervention performed immediately after delivery to accelerate placental separation and reduce PPH risk by over 60%. Its three components are:
1. Administer a uterotonic (Oxytocin 10 IU IM) within 1 minute of birth after palpating the abdomen to exclude a second baby.
2. Perform Controlled Cord Traction (CCT) during a contraction while applying upward counter-traction just above the symphysis pubis to guard against uterine inversion.
3. Assess uterine tone and massage gently if soft immediately after placental delivery.

(b) Following delivery of the placenta, the midwife must:
1. Palpate the uterine fundus every 15 minutes for the first 2 hours to confirm it stays firm, central, and well contracted (a boggy uterus indicates uterine atony).
2. Examine both maternal and fetal sides of the placenta plus all membranes on a flat tray to verify zero retained lobes or torn membranes.
3. Inspect the perineum, vagina, and cervix under good lighting to identify and suture bleeding lacerations, while charting blood loss, pulse, and blood pressure continuously.
es-mw-1.examinerTip: Always mention palpating the abdomen to rule out an undiagnosed second twin BEFORE giving Oxytocin 10 IU IM.

es-mw-2.topic: Newborn Assessment · APGAR Score & Neonatal Resuscitation
es-mw-2.prompt:
(a) List the five parameters assessed in the APGAR score and state the clinical interpretation of scores 7–10, 4–6, and 0–3. (6 marks)
(b) Outline the four urgent 'Golden Minute' steps when a newborn is born limp and not crying. (4 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Appearance (skin colour), Pulse (heart rate <100 vs >=100 bpm), Grimace (reflex irritability), Activity (muscle tone), Respiration (breathing effort) — 0, 1, or 2 pts each = 10 total (3 marks). Interpretation: 7–10 Normal routine care; 4–6 Moderate depression (stimulation/bag-mask oxygen); 0–3 Severe asphyxia (immediate resuscitation) (3 marks).

(b) Dry thoroughly & remove wet cloth/keep warm under radiant heater; Clear airway only if obstructed with visible secretions/meconium (avoid deep aggressive suction); Position head slightly extended ('sniffing position') & gently stimulate back/soles; If still apnoeic/gasping or HR < 100 bpm within 60 seconds, start positive-pressure Bag-and-Mask Ventilation at 40 breaths/min with room air (4 marks).
es-mw-2.modelAnswer:
(a) Measured at 1 and 5 minutes of life, APGAR evaluates five parameters scored 0–2 each (maximum 10): Appearance (colour), Pulse (heart rate >= 100 bpm = 2), Grimace (reflex response), Activity (flexed tone), and Respiration (vigorous cry). A total score of 7–10 indicates good adaptation; 4–6 indicates moderate depression requiring active stimulation/respiratory support; 0–3 indicates severe birth asphyxia demanding immediate full resuscitation.

(b) In the 'Golden Minute' for a non-breathing floppy newborn:
1. Dry rapidly with a warm towel, discard the wet cloth, and place skin-to-skin or under a pre-warmed radiant heater.
2. Open the airway in a neutral 'sniffing' position and clear visible secretions gently if obstructed.
3. Rub the baby's back gently 2–3 times; cut cord quickly if needed for resuscitation table transfer.
4. Before 60 seconds elapse, begin bag-and-mask ventilation with room air (approx. 40 breaths/min), watching for visible chest rise and rising heart rate >= 100 bpm.
es-mw-2.examinerTip: Do NOT wait for the 1-minute APGAR score to begin drying, opening airway, and bag-mask ventilation if the baby is limp and apnoeic at birth!

es-mw-3.topic: Obstetric Emergency · Severe Pre-eclampsia, Eclampsia & MgSO4 Toxicity
es-mw-3.prompt:
A 22-year-old primigravida at 36 weeks gestation presents with severe frontal headache, blurred vision, epigastric pain, BP 172/114 mmHg, Urine protein +++, and brisk knee reflexes. Ten minutes later she suffers a generalized tonic-clonic convulsion.
(a) State the diagnosis and differentiate Severe Pre-eclampsia from Eclampsia. (4 marks)
(b) Describe the Pritchard Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) loading and maintenance protocol alongside urgent antihypertensive care. (10 marks)
(c) Outline the three clinical safety observations required before EVERY repeat dose of MgSO4, and the emergency antidote if toxicity occurs. (8 marks)
(d) Explain definitive obstetric management once maternal seizures and BP are stabilized. (8 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Diagnosis: Eclampsia (evolving from severe pre-eclampsia with warning aura signs — headache, visual disturbance, epigastric pain, proteinuria +++, BP >= 160/110) (4 marks).

(b) Airway left-lateral recovery position + padded rails + O2 + IV access (2 marks); MgSO4 Loading dose (Pritchard): 4 g IV diluted over 10–15 min PLUS 10 g deep IM (5 g in each buttock with lignocaine) = 14 g total loading (4 marks); Maintenance: 5 g MgSO4 deep IM every 4 hours into alternating buttocks for 24 hrs post-delivery/last seizure (2 marks); Antihypertensive: IV Hydralazine 5 mg slow IV q20m (or oral Nifedipine 10–20 mg / IV Labetalol) targeting BP ~140–150 / 90–100 mmHg cleanly (not sudden drop risking placental hypoperfusion) (2 marks).

(c) Three mandatory pre-dose checks (2 marks each = 6 marks): 1) Respiratory Rate >= 16 breaths/min; 2) Patellar (knee-jerk) deep tendon reflexes PRESENT; 3) Urine Output >= 30 mL/hr (>= 100–120 mL over prior 4 hours). Antidote: Stop MgSO4 immediately and give Calcium Gluconate 10% (1 g / 10 mL) IV slowly over 3–5 minutes (2 marks).

(d) Delivery of the baby and placenta is the ONLY definitive cure for eclampsia (2 marks); Aim delivery within 12 hours once mother stabilized (avoid rushing unstabilized surgery during active convulsion) (2 marks); Assess cervix (Bishop score) — induce/augment labour with vaginal delivery if favourable/fetal heart normal, or urgent Caesarean section if unfavourable/fetal distress (2 marks); Monitor closely postpartum for PPH, pulmonary oedema, HELLP syndrome, and keep MgSO4 going for 24 hrs postpartum (2 marks).
es-mw-3.modelAnswer:
(a) The patient now has Eclampsia (new-onset generalized tonic-clonic seizures in a woman with severe pre-eclampsia: BP >= 160/110 mmHg, +++ proteinuria, and cerebral/hepatic end-organ symptoms like headache, blurred vision, and epigastric pain).

(b) First place her in the left-lateral recovery position, clear the airway, apply high-flow oxygen, and prevent injury without forcing objects into her mouth. Insert a large-bore IV cannula and draw blood for CBC/platelets, renal, and liver function tests.
Administer Magnesium Sulfate (Pritchard regimen) immediately:
• Loading Dose (14 g total): 4 g of 20% MgSO4 slow IV over 10–15 minutes PLUS 10 g of 50% MgSO4 deep IM (5 g into upper outer quadrant of each buttock).
• Maintenance Dose: 5 g deep IM every 4 hours into alternating buttocks continuing for 24 hours after delivery or last fit.
Lower dangerous blood pressure gradually with IV Hydralazine 5 mg slow IV every 20 minutes (or oral Nifedipine/IV Labetalol) aiming for ~140–150/90–100 mmHg to prevent maternal stroke without compromising placental perfusion.

(c) Before administering EVERY 4-hourly maintenance dose of MgSO4, verify all three safety thresholds:
1. Respiratory rate >= 16 breaths/min.
2. Patellar (knee-jerk) reflex present.
3. Urine output >= 30 mL/hr (at least 100–120 mL over the past 4 hours).
If any threshold fails, HOLD MgSO4 and administer Calcium Gluconate 10% (10 mL = 1 g) slow IV immediately while supporting respiration.

(d) Delivery of the fetus and placenta is the definitive cure. Once maternal seizures and blood pressure are stabilized, plan delivery within 12 hours: favour vaginal birth (induction/arm) if cervix is ripe and fetal heart reassuring, or perform Caesarean section under safe anaesthesia if cervix unfavourable or fetal distress exists. Continue ICU/HDU monitoring for 24–48 hours postpartum for pulmonary oedema, PPH, and HELLP syndrome.
es-mw-3.examinerTip: Write all 3 MgSO4 toxicity checks AND the Calcium Gluconate 10% 1 g IV antidote verbatim — this appears in virtually every Ugandan Midwifery UNMEB paper!

es-ph-1.topic: Community Health Nursing · Home Visiting Process
es-ph-1.prompt:
(a) Define Home Visiting in Community Health Nursing. (2 marks)
(b) State and briefly describe the five (5) sequential phases of a planned home visit. (8 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Purposeful family-centred nursing service delivered inside a client's home environment to assess health needs, provide care, and educate using available household resources (2 marks).

(b) 1.6 marks per phase: 1) Initiation / Planning phase (review family record, prepare home-visit bag, clarify purpose); 2) Introductory / Entry phase (greet respectfully, establish rapport, explain reason for visit); 3) Implementation / Action phase (carry out clinical assessment, nursing procedures, health education tailored to home setup); 4) Evaluation phase (check family understanding, review objectives met); 5) Termination & Documentation phase (summarize next steps, schedule follow-up date, record visit accurately).
es-ph-1.modelAnswer:
(a) Home visiting is a planned, purposeful community nursing process delivered to an individual or family within their home setting to assess holistic health status, promote preventive practices, and provide nursing care using household resources.

(b) The five sequential phases are:
1. Planning / Pre-visit Phase: Review prior family health records, verify objectives, and pack sterile equipment inside the community nursing bag.
2. Initiation / Entry Phase: Knock respectfully, greet family elders appropriately, introduce yourself, and state the visit purpose to build trust.
3. Implementation Phase: Perform physical/environmental assessment, deliver hands-on care (e.g. postnatal check, MUAC screening, wound care), and offer culturally sensitive health education.
4. Evaluation Phase: Ask the caregiver to teach back key instructions and assess whether planned health outcomes are being met.
5. Termination & Documentation Phase: Agree on a follow-up return date or referral, bid farewell politely, and document all findings and actions promptly.
es-ph-1.examinerTip: List the phases strictly in chronological order (Planning -> Initiation -> Implementation -> Evaluation -> Termination/Recording).

es-ph-2.prompt:
A 14-month-old child (weight 10 kg) presents with acute watery diarrhoea x 3 days, lethargy, sunken eyes, inability to drink, and skin pinch going back very slowly (> 2 seconds).
(a) Classify the child's hydration status under IMCI guidelines. (2 marks)
(b) Calculate and outline the exact IV Ringer's Lactate volume and infusion schedule under WHO/UCG Plan C for this 10 kg infant (> 12 months). (8 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Severe Dehydration (Pink classification) — requires immediate IMCI Plan C urgent IV rehydration (2 marks).
(b) Total Plan C volume = 100 mL/kg = 100 × 10 kg = 1,000 mL Ringer's Lactate given over 3 hours because child is >= 12 months (1 mark for 100 mL/kg total = 1,000 mL).
(b) Step 1 bolus (30 mL/kg over 30 minutes for child >= 12 months): 30 × 10 kg = 300 mL Ringer's Lactate in 30 minutes (3 marks).
(b) Step 2 remainder (70 mL/kg over 2.5 hours): 70 × 10 kg = 700 mL Ringer's Lactate over 2.5 hours (2 marks).

(b) Monitoring & follow-up: Reassess pulse/cap refill after first 30 min (repeat 30 mL/kg if radial pulse still weak/absent), begin oral ORS 5 mL/kg/hr + Zinc 20 mg/day x 10 days as soon as child can drink safely, and reassess after 3 hours (2 marks).
es-ph-2.modelAnswer:
(a) Under IMCI, two or more red-flag signs (lethargic, sunken eyes, unable to drink, skin pinch > 2 seconds) classify this child as having Severe Dehydration (Pink Row), requiring immediate Plan C intravenous resuscitation.

(b) Because the child is 14 months old (>= 12 months) and weighs 10 kg, total Ringer's Lactate required under Plan C is 100 mL/kg = 1,000 mL infused over 3 hours in two phases:
• Phase 1 (First 30 minutes): Give 30 mL/kg = 300 mL IV rapidly over 30 minutes. Reassess immediately; if radial pulse remains weak or absent, repeat 300 mL.
• Phase 2 (Next 2½ hours): Give 70 mL/kg = 700 mL IV over 2 hours 30 minutes.
Also monitor urine output, check blood glucose for hypoglycaemia, offer ORS (5 mL/kg/hr) once alert enough to drink, and administer Oral Zinc 20 mg once daily for 10 days.
es-ph-2.examinerTip: Remember the crucial IMCI age split: Infant < 12 months gets 30 mL/kg over 1 hr + 70 mL/kg over 5 hrs (= 6 hrs total); Child >= 12 months gets 30 mL/kg over 30 min + 70 mL/kg over 2.5 hrs (= 3 hrs total)!

es-ph-3.topic: Paediatrics & Nutrition · Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) & Primary Health Care
es-ph-3.prompt:
A 2-year-old child presents at the nutrition ward with bilateral pitting pedal oedema, thin sparse reddish hair, flaking 'flaky-paint' skin lesions, misery/apathy, and MUAC 10.8 cm.
(a) Identify the condition and compare four clinical features distinguishing Kwashiorkor from Marasmus. (8 marks)
(b) State the first five (5) WHO '10 Steps' Stabilization priorities during Days 1–2 and explain why IV fluids and iron are avoided initially. (12 marks)
(c) Outline five Primary Health Care strategies to prevent malnutrition in Ugandan communities. (10 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Kwashiorkor / Oedematous Severe Acute Malnutrition (MUAC < 11.5 cm + bilateral oedema). Comparison table: Kwashiorkor (bilateral pitting oedema, moon face, flaky-paint dermatitis, sparse discoloured hair, enlarged fatty liver, miserable/apathetic, severe hypoalbuminaemia) vs Marasmus (no oedema, severe muscle/fat wasting 'old man face', sunken eyes/ribs visible, alert/irritable, voracious appetite, extreme weight-for-height deficit) (8 marks).

(b) WHO Steps 1–5 (2 marks each = 10 marks): Step 1 Hypoglycaemia (feed F-75 q2h or 10% Dextrose 5 mL/kg IV/oral immediately if < 3.0 mmol/L); Step 2 Hypothermia (kangaroo/warm room, keep dry/covered, axillary T >= 35.5°C); Step 3 Dehydration (Give ReSoMal orally/NGT slowly, AVOID routine IV fluids unless frank shock because fragile heart risks fatal fluid overload/heart failure); Step 4 Electrolyte imbalance (supplement Potassium & Magnesium in F-75; NEVER add extra Sodium); Step 5 Infection (start broad-spectrum antibiotics — e.g. Ampicillin + Gentamicin — even if no fever present because SAM blunts febrile response). Iron rule (2 marks): Wait until Rehabilitation Phase (after Day 7/appetite returns) because free iron promotes bacterial growth and oxidative free-radical damage during stabilization.

(c) Exclusive breastfeeding 0–6 months + timely nutrient-dense complementary feeding using locally available foods ('Kitobero'/beans/silverfish/greens); Routine UNEPI immunisation (especially Measles/Vitamin A); Early growth monitoring (MUAC & Road-to-Health charts at outreach clinics); Safe water, sanitation & deworming (WASH); Maternal nutrition education & birth spacing (10 marks).
es-ph-3.modelAnswer:
(a) The child has Kwashiorkor (Oedematous Severe Acute Malnutrition, confirmed by bilateral pitting oedema and MUAC 10.8 cm < 11.5 cm).
Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus:
• Oedema: Present bilaterally (feet/sacrum/face) in Kwashiorkor; Absent in Marasmus.
• Hair & Skin: Sparse hypopigmented hair + 'flaky paint' dermatosis in Kwashiorkor; dry loose wrinkled skin ('old man face' & baggy pants buttocks) in Marasmus.
• Mood & Appetite: Apathetic/miserable with anorexia in Kwashiorkor; alert/irritable with strong appetite initially in Marasmus.
• Liver: Hepatomegaly (fatty liver) common in Kwashiorkor; rare in Marasmus.

(b) WHO Stabilization Priorities (Days 1–2):
1. Treat/Prevent Hypoglycaemia: Start 2-hourly F-75 feeds immediately (treat glucose < 3.0 mmol/L with 10% Dextrose 5 mL/kg).
2. Treat/Prevent Hypothermia: Warm skin-to-skin/blankets and keep rooms draught-free.
3. Correct Dehydration Carefully: Rehydrate orally/NGT using special low-sodium ReSoMal; avoid routine IV fluids unless true shock occurs because an atrophic malnourished myocardium quickly develops fatal heart failure/pulmonary oedema.
4. Correct Electrolytes: Provide high potassium and magnesium in F-75 while keeping sodium strictly low.
5. Treat Presumed Infection: Give empiric IV Ampicillin + Gentamicin routinely even without fever, because malnourished children lack inflammatory fever responses.
*Note on Iron:* Withhold iron during the Stabilization phase until active infection clears and appetite returns (~Day 7/Rehabilitation F-100 phase), as free iron encourages bacterial proliferation and worsens sepsis.

(c) PHC Prevention Strategies:
1. Promote exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months and fortified local complementary 'Kitobero' mixtures thereafter.
2. Complete routine UNEPI immunizations (particularly Measles vaccine) and 6-monthly Vitamin A supplementation.
3. Monthly growth monitoring (Road-to-Health weight/height + community MUAC screening by VHTs).
4. Safe drinking water, household latrines, handwashing, and routine deworming (Albendazole/Mebendazole).
5. Family planning education for healthy child spacing and kitchen gardening support.
es-ph-3.examinerTip: Memorize the TWO classic SAM examiner trap questions: (1) Why avoid IV fluids in dehydrated SAM? -> Risk of cardiac failure! (2) Why withhold iron in week 1? -> Feeds bacteria & increases sepsis mortality!

anat1-heart.section: Section C — Long Clinical Anatomy Essay
anat1-heart.topic: Cardiovascular Anatomy · Chambers, Valves & Coronary Circulation
anat1-heart.prompt:
(a) Trace the sequential pathway of blood through the four chambers, four valves, and pulmonary/systemic vessels starting at the Vena Cava. (10 marks)
(b) Name the two main arteries supplying the myocardium and explain why left ventricular infarction rapidly leads to pulmonary oedema. (10 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Superior/Inferior Vena Cava -> Right Atrium -> Tricuspid valve -> Right Ventricle -> Pulmonary semilunar valve -> Pulmonary arteries -> Lungs -> Pulmonary veins -> Left Atrium -> Bicuspid (Mitral) valve -> Left Ventricle -> Aortic semilunar valve -> Aorta -> Systemic tissues (10 marks, ~1 mark per step).

(b) Left and Right Coronary Arteries arising directly from the ascending aorta immediately above the aortic semilunar cusps (3 marks); Impaired Left Ventricle pumping increases Left Atrial and Pulmonary Venous hydrostatic pressure (4 marks); Fluid crosses alveolar-capillary membranes causing acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema (pink frothy sputum, orthopnoea, basal crackles) (3 marks).
anat1-heart.modelAnswer:
(a) Deoxygenated venous blood drains via the Superior and Inferior Venae Cavae (plus Coronary Sinus) into the Right Atrium, crosses the Tricuspid (right atrioventricular) valve into the Right Ventricle, passes through the Pulmonary semilunar valve into the pulmonary trunk/arteries to undergo oxygenation in alveolar capillaries. Oxygenated blood returns via four Pulmonary Veins into the Left Atrium, flows across the Mitral (Bicuspid) valve into the thick-walled Left Ventricle, and is ejected past the Aortic semilunar valve into the Aorta for systemic perfusion.

(b) The myocardium is perfused during ventricular diastole by the Right and Left Coronary Arteries branching immediately above the aortic valve. When an acute myocardial infarction weakens Left Ventricular contractility, end-diastolic volume and pressure rise backward into the Left Atrium and pulmonary veins, elevating pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure above colloid osmotic pressure and forcing serous fluid into alveoli—producing flash pulmonary oedema.
anat1-heart.examinerTip: Explicitly state that coronary arteries fill during DIASTOLE, and distinguish tricuspid (right AV) from mitral/bicuspid (left AV) clearly.

anat1-respiratory.prompt:
(a) Describe the structural features of the respiratory membrane allowing rapid gas exchange. (5 marks)
(b) State the cellular source and physiological function of pulmonary surfactant in premature neonates. (5 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Ultra-thin Type I alveolar squamous epithelium + fused basement membrane + thin capillary endothelium (~0.5 um thickness); Vast surface area (~70 m2); Moist surfactant-lined surface; Rich capillary network (5 marks).

(b) Secreted by Type II pneumocytes (septal cells) starting around 24–34 weeks gestation (2 marks); Reduces alveolar surface tension to prevent alveolar collapse (atelectasis) on expiration; Deficiency causes Infant Respiratory Distress Syndrome (Hyaline Membrane Disease) treated with CPAP & surfactant/antenatal Dexamethasone (3 marks).
anat1-respiratory.modelAnswer:
(a) Rapid passive diffusion of O2 and CO2 occurs across the respiratory membrane (~0.5 micrometres thin), formed by Type I simple squamous alveolar epithelial cells, fused epithelial-capillary basement membranes, and thin pulmonary capillary endothelium, supported by ~300 million alveoli providing ~70 m2 of moist gas-exchange area.

(b) Pulmonary surfactant is a phospholipid-protein complex synthesized by Type II alveolar cells. By lowering liquid surface tension inside alveoli, surfactant maintains alveolar stability, improves lung compliance, and prevents collapse at end-expiration. Preterm infants (< 34 weeks) lack adequate surfactant and develop Respiratory Distress Syndrome (tachypnoea, nasal flaring, grunting, intercostal recessions).
anat1-respiratory.examinerTip: Identify Type I cells = gas diffusion, Type II cells = surfactant production, and alveolar macrophages = dust phagocytosis.

anat2-nephron.section: Section C — Long Clinical Anatomy Essay
anat2-nephron.prompt:
(a) List the segments of a renal nephron in order and explain the three physiological processes that form urine. (12 marks)
(b) Describe how Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH / Vasopressin) regulates plasma osmolarity during dehydration. (8 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Glomerulus & Bowman's capsule -> Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) -> Loop of Henle (descending & ascending limbs) -> Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT) -> Collecting Duct (4 marks). Processes: 1) Glomerular Filtration (hydrostatic pressure drives water/small solutes minus plasma proteins across fenestrated capillaries, GFR ~125 mL/min); 2) Tubular Reabsorption (selective recovery of ~99% water, 100% glucose, Na+, amino acids mainly in PCT); 3) Tubular Secretion (active H+, K+, NH4+, creatinine, drug metabolite elimination into filtrate for acid-base control) (8 marks).

(b) Dehydration raises plasma osmolarity -> hypothalamic osmoreceptors shrink and stimulate posterior pituitary ADH release (3 marks); ADH inserts aquaporin-2 water channels into DCT/Collecting Duct principal cells -> increases passive water reabsorption back into medullary blood (3 marks); Urine becomes concentrated (dark yellow, small volume), restoring circulating volume and diluting plasma back to 285–295 mOsm/kg (2 marks).
anat2-nephron.modelAnswer:
(a) Urine passes sequentially from the Glomerulus and Bowman's Capsule into the Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT), Loop of Henle, Distal Convoluted Tubule (DCT), and Collecting Duct. Three coordinated steps form urine:
1. Glomerular Filtration: Arterial hydrostatic pressure forces protein-free plasma filtrate (~180 L/day) through the glomerular filtration membrane.
2. Tubular Reabsorption: ~65% of water, sodium, and virtually 100% of filtered glucose and amino acids are reclaimed into peritubular capillaries primarily in the PCT.
3. Tubular Secretion: Hydrogen ions, potassium, ammonia, and drugs (e.g. penicillins) are actively transported from blood into the tubule lumen to maintain plasma pH 7.35–7.45.

(b) When dehydration raises blood osmolarity, hypothalamic osmoreceptors signal the posterior pituitary gland to secrete ADH (arginine vasopressin). ADH binds V2 receptors on late DCT and collecting duct cells, triggering insertion of aquaporin-2 water channels. Water moves osmotically out into the hypertonic renal medulla, lowering urine volume, increasing urine specific gravity, and restoring normal plasma osmolarity.
anat2-nephron.examinerTip: State normal GFR (~125 mL/min) and always clarify that ADH is synthesized in the HYPOTHALAMUS and stored/released by the POSTERIOR PITUITARY.

anat2-cranial.prompt:
(a) Match Cranial Nerves I, II, III, VII, VIII, and X with their primary motor or sensory clinical functions. (6 marks)
(b) State two functions of Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) and the anatomical site for safe lumbar puncture in adults. (4 marks)
markingPoints: (a) I Olfactory (smell), II Optic (visual acuity/fields), III Oculomotor (pupil constriction & eye movement), VII Facial (facial expression muscles & anterior tongue taste), VIII Vestibulocochlear (hearing & equilibrium), X Vagus (parasympathetic thorax/abdomen, gag reflex, swallowing/voice) (6 marks).

(b) CSF Functions: Mechanical buoyancy cushioning brain/spinal cord against trauma; chemical homeostasis/nutrient delivery & metabolic waste clearance (2 marks). Adult LP site: Subarachnoid space at L3–L4 or L4–L5 interspace (safely below conus medullaris terminating at L1–L2) (2 marks).
anat2-cranial.modelAnswer:
(a) Key cranial nerve functions: CN I (Olfactory) mediates smell; CN II (Optic) transmits vision; CN III (Oculomotor) controls pupillary constriction (PERRLA) and extraocular eye movement; CN VII (Facial) supplies facial expression muscles and anterior 2/3 taste; CN VIII (Vestibulocochlear) governs hearing and balance; CN X (Vagus) regulates swallowing, speech phonation, gag reflex, and parasympathetic cardiac/GI tone.

(b) CSF cushions the brain mechanically through buoyancy and clears metabolic waste while distributing electrolytes. In adults, diagnostic lumbar puncture enters the L3–L4 or L4–L5 intervertebral space, safely below the conus medullaris termination at L1–L2.
anat2-cranial.examinerTip: Remember: L1–L2 is where the adult spinal cord ends, which is why L3–L4 / L4–L5 prevents spinal cord injury.

anat2-endocrine.topic: Endocrine System · Insulin vs Glucagon & Thyroid
anat2-endocrine.prompt:
(a) Contrast the opposing actions of Insulin and Glucagon on blood glucose regulation. (6 marks)
(b) Explain four classic symptoms of Hyperthyroidism (Thyrotoxicosis) based on cellular metabolism. (4 marks)
markingPoints: (a) Insulin (pancreatic beta-cells): Lowers blood glucose post-meal via GLUT-4 muscle/adipose uptake, liver glycogenesis, and lipogenesis (3 marks). Glucagon (pancreatic alpha-cells): Raises blood glucose during fasting via hepatic glycogenolysis & gluconeogenesis (3 marks).

(b) 1 mark each: Weight loss despite increased appetite (hypercatabolism), Heat intolerance & profuse sweating (elevated BMR thermogenesis), Tachycardia/palpitations (beta-adrenergic receptor upregulation), Fine hand tremors/anxiety/exophthalmos (sympathetic overactivity/autoimmune orbital inflammation).
anat2-endocrine.modelAnswer:
(a) Pancreatic beta-cells secrete Insulin when blood glucose rises, stimulating peripheral glucose uptake, hepatic glycogenesis, and fat storage to lower plasma glucose. Conversely, alpha-cells release Glucagon during fasting or hypoglycaemia, triggering hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis to elevate circulating glucose back to 3.9–5.5 mmol/L.

(b) Excess thyroid hormones T3/T4 raise basal metabolic rate and sympathetic sensitivity, causing: (1) unintended weight loss despite hyperphagia; (2) heat intolerance and sweating from increased cellular thermogenesis; (3) resting tachycardia or palpitations; and (4) fine tremor, restlessness, or lid lag/exophthalmos (in Graves' disease).
anat2-endocrine.examinerTip: Always name the Islet cell types: Beta cells = Insulin, Alpha cells = Glucagon.

fond1-ipc.topic: Infection Prevention & Control (IPC) · Chain of Infection & Hand Hygiene
fond1-ipc.prompt:
(a) Draw or list in sequence the six links of the Chain of Infection and give one nursing measure to break EACH link. (12 marks)
(b) State WHO's 'Five Moments for Hand Hygiene' and compare Alcohol-Based Hand Rub vs Soap & Water indications. (8 marks)
markingPoints: (a) 2 marks per link + break: 1) Infectious Agent (prompt diagnosis/antimicrobials/disinfection); 2) Reservoir (proper waste segregation, clean linen, handwashing, wound dressing); 3) Portal of Exit (masks/cough etiquette, sealing drainage bags, gloves on body fluids); 4) Mode of Transmission (hand hygiene, isolation/transmission precautions, sterilization); 5) Portal of Entry (aseptic catheter insertion/sterile dressing/protect broken skin); 6) Susceptible Host (immunization, adequate nutrition, glycemic/chronic control) (12 marks).

(b) WHO 5 Moments: 1) Before touching a patient; 2) Before clean/aseptic procedure; 3) After body fluid exposure risk; 4) After touching a patient; 5) After touching patient surroundings (5 marks).
